Docs / Operations

Troubleshooting

Preserve the failing operation, exact message, task ID, and revision. Repeating an unchanged launch is not recovery.

Installation or wrong project

Require Node 22+. Open a new terminal after installation or use the installed shim. Check the directory and ATL_PROJECT before initialization or changes. A reused URL may serve a different project; inspect its process and title.

Issues are missing

Inspect source enablement, base/collection URL, project/repository selection, and authentication in the server environment. Saving, previewing, and importing are separate steps. Follow issue sources.

Plan approval fails

Read unresolved questions, findings, artifact version, source revision, and review binding. Update and review the artifact instead of retrying stale evidence. See plan contract.

Queue is blocked

Use atl why T-001 for the actual task. Inspect prerequisites, handoffs, provider readiness, approvals, and allowance. Preserve the blocker and follow queue recovery.

Provider stops or quota fails

Inspect error and run state. Confirm a fallback is permitted, ready, and capable. Unknown capacity and missing tokens remain unknown. See providers and execution reports.

Ask ATL does not fix work

Check discussion versus fix mode, approval of the exact request, and workspace access. Contextual conversation alone does not authorize execution or satisfy review. See Ask ATL.

A task has no useful diff

Inspect its source baseline and output capture. A missing baseline cannot be honestly replaced with arbitrary current HEAD. See change review.

Search or diagrams fail

Run npm ci, npm run docs:build, and npm run docs:check. Use npm run docs:serve instead of file:. Inspect browser errors and retain the page and diagram source when reporting a failure.

Report a reproducible problem

Include expected/actual behavior, minimal synthetic input, command, revision, verifier output, and affected source boundary. Remove credentials and private issue content before sharing.
